observation_text: Child became upset when parent left the room during playtime.
antecedent: Parent left the room to answer a phone call.
behavior: Child started crying and ran to find the parent.
consequence: Child calmed down and continued playing once parent returned.
caregiver_response: Parent reassured the child that they would be back soon.
suggested_followup_question: How can we help them feel more secure during these moments?
general_support_idea: Offering comfort items during separations.

observation_text: Child hesitated to join the group at school after arrival.
antecedent: Classmates were already playing games.
behavior: Child stood by the door and watched without joining in.
consequence: No consequence noted
caregiver_response: Teacher gently encouraged the child to join a friend.
suggested_followup_question: What strategies can encourage them to engage?
general_support_idea: Creating small group activities to ease participation.

observation_text: Child clung to the caregiver at a family gathering.
antecedent: Many relatives were present and socializing.
behavior: Child held onto caregiver's leg and wouldn't let go.
consequence: Caregiver picked the child up and moved to a quieter area.
caregiver_response: Caregiver offered a snack to distract the child.
suggested_followup_question: What can we do to help them feel more comfortable in new situations?
general_support_idea: Encouraging familiar activities in busy settings.

observation_text: Child expressed reluctance to go outside after a brief rain.
antecedent: Weather changed suddenly.
behavior: Child stood at the door and refused to go out.
consequence: No consequence noted
caregiver_response: Parent offered to go out with the child.
suggested_followup_question: What activities can we do indoors to keep them engaged?
general_support_idea: Exploring indoor games together.

observation_text: Child became anxious waiting in line at the store.
antecedent: Child saw a long line and many people.
behavior: Child started fidgeting and asked if they could leave.
consequence: Caregiver offered to play a game while waiting.
caregiver_response: Parent suggested counting items on the shelves together.
suggested_followup_question: How can we make waiting more fun for them?
general_support_idea: Using distraction techniques during waits.

observation_text: Child refused to enter the classroom for the first day.
antecedent: New school year began.
behavior: Child stood outside the door and shook their head.
consequence: Teacher knelt down and spoke to the child, encouraging them to try.
caregiver_response: Teacher offered to introduce the child to a classmate.
suggested_followup_question: What can we do before school starts to ease their transition?
general_support_idea: Visiting the classroom beforehand.

observation_text: Child wandered away from the caregiver in a crowded park.
antecedent: Family arrived at a busy park.
behavior: Child ran towards the playground without looking back.
consequence: Caregiver quickly called the child back and explained staying close.
caregiver_response: Caregiver reinforced the importance of staying together.
suggested_followup_question: How can we ensure their safety in busy places?
general_support_idea: Setting clear boundaries about exploring.

observation_text: Child was upset when a caregiver left for a short errand.
antecedent: Caregiver prepared to leave the house.
behavior: Child cried and followed the caregiver to the door.
consequence: Child settled down with a toy after caregiver left.
caregiver_response: Caregiver promised a quick return.
suggested_followup_question: What can we do to reassure them during these times?
general_support_idea: Using a timer to indicate return time.

observation_text: Child hesitated to join a friend at the playground.
antecedent: Friend called them over to play.
behavior: Child stood still and looked unsure.
consequence: Child eventually walked over after seeing the friend wave.
caregiver_response: Caregiver encouraged the child to give it a try.
suggested_followup_question: What can help them feel more confident in social settings?
general_support_idea: Role-playing social interactions at home.

observation_text: Child locked themselves in the bathroom when left alone.
antecedent: Caregiver asked the child to take a break.
behavior: Child locked the door and wouldn't come out when called.
consequence: Caregiver knocked and reassured the child that they were safe.
possible_trigger: Being left alone for a moment
emotion_context: Desire for control in a stressful moment
caregiver_response: Caregiver gently opened the door to check on them.
suggested_followup_question: How can we prevent such situations in the future?
general_support_idea: Discussing feelings about being alone.

observation_text: Child showed reluctance to leave a friend's house after playing.
antecedent: Time to go home was announced.
behavior: Child sat down and refused to move from the floor.
consequence: Caregiver offered to pick up the child and carry them out.
emotion_context: Not wanting to leave fun activities
caregiver_response: Caregiver explained the next fun activity at home.
suggested_followup_question: What can we do to ease transitions between activities?
general_support_idea: Making a visual schedule of the day.

observation_text: Child cried at a restaurant when the food took too long.
antecedent: Waiting for food to arrive.
behavior: Child started whimpering and looking around nervously.
consequence: Caregiver offered a toy to distract the child until the food arrived.
caregiver_response: Caregiver reassured the child that food would be there soon.
suggested_followup_question: What can we do to manage their expectations when waiting?
general_support_idea: Bringing activities for waiting periods.

observation_text: Child clung to the caregiver during a school drop-off.
antecedent: Arriving at school after break.
behavior: Child held tightly to the caregiver's hand and wouldn't let go.
consequence: Caregiver knelt down to assure the child it was safe to go in.
possible_trigger: Returning to school after a break
caregiver_response: Caregiver encouraged them to say goodbye to friends.
suggested_followup_question: How can we make drop-offs smoother for them?
general_support_idea: Practicing short separations at home.

observation_text: Child refused to walk into the public transport area.
antecedent: Transitioning from one bus to another.
behavior: Child stood at the entrance and looked around anxiously.
consequence: Caregiver guided the child and explained the process of boarding.
caregiver_response: Caregiver promised to stay close and count the stops together.
suggested_followup_question: What can we do to help with public transport experiences?
general_support_idea: Creating a checklist for boarding.

observation_text: Child continuously asked when they could go home while playing outside.
antecedent: Family was at a picnic.
behavior: Child kept looking at the exit and asking about leaving.
consequence: Caregiver suggested playing a game to pass the time.
caregiver_response: Caregiver encouraged the child to enjoy the moment.
suggested_followup_question: What can we do to help them enjoy being outside?
general_support_idea: Bringing favorite toys for outdoor play.

observation_text: Child refused to enter the public library due to a crowd of visitors.
antecedent: Arriving at a busy library event.
behavior: Child stood outside and shook their head, refusing to go in.
consequence: Caregiver offered to explore the outside area first.
caregiver_response: Caregiver prompted a discussion about what they could enjoy inside.
suggested_followup_question: What strategies can we use for visits to crowded places?
general_support_idea: Planning visits during less busy times.

observation_text: Child would not leave the playground after many requests.
antecedent: Time to go home was approaching.
behavior: Child sat on the structure and ignored requests to come down.
consequence: Caregiver approached calmly and offered a countdown to leave.
caregiver_response: Caregiver set a timer for five minutes before heading home.
suggested_followup_question: What can we do to improve transition times?
general_support_idea: Setting clear end times before play.

observation_text: Child expressed discomfort when family visited unexpectedly.
antecedent: Unfamiliar guests arrived.
behavior: Child hid behind a parent and peeked out occasionally.
consequence: Child gradually approached the guests after some reassurance.
caregiver_response: Caregiver introduced the child to the guests gently.
suggested_followup_question: How can we prepare them for unexpected situations?
general_support_idea: Discussing visitors before they arrive.

observation_text: Child became anxious when separated from a caregiver at the grocery store.
antecedent: Caregiver stopped to look at items on a shelf.
behavior: Child wandered off a few feet and looked back with worry.
consequence: Child quickly returned when the caregiver called them.
caregiver_response: Caregiver reminded the child to stay close while shopping.
suggested_followup_question: What can we do to reinforce safety in stores?
general_support_idea: Practicing staying close during trips.

observation_text: Child locked themselves in their room during a family gathering.
antecedent: Loud music and conversations were happening.
behavior: Child barricaded the door and wouldn't respond when called.
consequence: Caregiver managed to enter and talked softly to the child.
caregiver_response: Caregiver suggested a quiet space to relax together.
suggested_followup_question: How can we help them cope with loud situations?
general_support_idea: Creating a safe space in busy environments.

observation_text: Child noticed their parent leaving the room and started calling out for them loudly.
antecedent: Parent prepared to leave for work.
behavior: Child ran to the door and grabbed their parent’s leg, refusing to let go.
consequence: Parent knelt down and reassured the child, and they both talked about plans for the day.
caregiver_response: Parent offered to play a game later together.
suggested_followup_question: How did the child respond after you reassured them?
general_support_idea: Provide a familiar object for comfort during transitions.

observation_text: Child was playing at daycare and saw other children being picked up by their parents.
antecedent: End of the day at daycare.
behavior: Child became visibly upset and sat on the floor, refusing to join the line for pick-up.
consequence: Child eventually joined the line after a friend offered them a toy to play with.
caregiver_response: Caregiver encouraged them to say goodbye to friends before leaving.
suggested_followup_question: Have you discussed the day's activities with the child?
general_support_idea: Encourage saying goodbye to friends during pick-up.

observation_text: Child was at the playground but wouldn't leave the play structure to go home.
antecedent: Playtime ending and the caregiver called for the child.
behavior: Child climbed higher on the structure and said they wanted to stay longer.
consequence: Child came down after the caregiver counted to three and reminded them of dinner plans.
caregiver_response: Caregiver provided a countdown to prepare for leaving.
suggested_followup_question: What strategies can we use to signal it's time to go next time?
general_support_idea: Use a visual timer for transitions.

observation_text: Child was in the store and saw a toy they wanted while the caregiver was busy with shopping.
antecedent: Caregiver focused on items to purchase.
behavior: Child wandered off to look at the toy aisle without telling the caregiver.
consequence: Caregiver quickly found the child and talked about safety rules, reminding them to stay close.
caregiver_response: Caregiver emphasized the importance of staying nearby.
suggested_followup_question: How can we make sure the child stays close in busy places?
general_support_idea: Practice staying together in familiar areas before shopping.

observation_text: Child was playing outside during a family gathering and started to walk away from the group.
antecedent: Lots of people and noise around.
behavior: Child began walking towards the street, seemingly unaware of surroundings.
consequence: Caregiver called out and walked quickly to intercept the child before they reached the street.
possible_trigger: Noise and activity of the gathering
caregiver_response: Caregiver explained why they need to stay close and suggested a game to play together.
suggested_followup_question: What can we do to help keep the child engaged during gatherings?
general_support_idea: Set up a designated play area nearby.
